2814.name: ravenrs_movie
2814.docs:
# ravenrs-movie

Training videos of a RavenRS app, small enough to ship inside it.

A film here has no pixels. It stores what the app drew, the same rectangles and shaped text the
renderer gets, so it stays sharp at any size and zoom, and a minute costs kilobytes instead of
megabytes. Built-in fonts are referenced, not copied.

**Recording** runs the real app from a script. The script clicks by the names screen readers see,
so it needs no GPU and no permission from the system, and it runs again when the screens change.

```rust,ignore
use ravenrs_movie::Recorder;

let mut take = Recorder::new(app, Theme::raven_light(), Size::new(1200.0, 760.0));
take.chapter("A new expense", "How to write down what you spent.");
take.note("Balance", "Your balance", "The sum of all accounts.", 2.0)?;
take.guide("New", "Open the menu", "Click New to begin.")?;
take.click("New")?;
take.type_into("Description", "Groceries")?;
std::fs::write("manual.ravenmovie", take.finish()?.to_bytes())?;
```

**Editing** is non-destructive, in the style of a screen-recording editor. A `Project` is a list of
clips and of overlays on tracks: cuts, speed, title cards, callouts, captions, spotlight, hiding
what should not show, zoom and pan, fades and a highlight around the pointer. `MovieEditor` is its
timeline, canvas and properties. The edits travel with the film, so there is nothing to render.

**Watching** is `MoviePlayer`, with chapters, a position bar and steps that wait for a click:

| What the script says | What it becomes in the player |
|---|---|
| `chapter` | An entry in the list of chapters |
| `note` | A mark on the screen whose text appears while it plays, and again on a click |
| `guide` | The film stops and waits for a click on that spot |
| `intro` | A chapter, with a box in the middle of the film saying what it teaches |
| `explain` | A `note` that lasts as long as its text takes to read or hear |

Whatever the film is saying shows in a box next to what it talks about, and a film too small for the
box has the words under it.

**Hearing** needs nothing in the file. Clicks and keys are noted while recording and their sounds are
computed, and the system's own voice reads each box in the language of the labels, so a film weighs
the same with sound as without. `MoviePlayer` has a switch for each. Recording runs with no window,
so the click is not captured from a real mouse: it is a click sound made to fit. On Linux the voice
needs `espeak-ng`; without it, the boxes still say it all.

**Asking** is `MovieAssistant`. Someone types a question and picks an answer, and the film opens at
that moment, with the answers out of the way. A step opens waiting for its click; anything else
plays from there.

```rust,ignore
use ravenrs_movie::{MovieAssistant, MovieLibrary};

let library = MovieLibrary::new().film("Manual", movie);
let assistant = MovieAssistant::new(library).width(960.0);
```

It searches the words the films hold, the chapters and the steps, ignoring accents and case, and it
accepts near forms of a word ("pago" finds "pagar") and typing slips. There is no model and nothing
leaves the machine, so it adds nothing to download and works in the browser. It knows no synonyms: a
question with no word in common with the films gets no answer, and it says so.

`MovieChat` is the same search as a conversation, for a `FloatingPanel` over the app. Each answer is
a card with the moments, and the app decides how to open them. `MovieChat::writer` lets a local
model write the answer about what the search found; finding stays with the search, and a question
that finds nothing never reaches the model.

`MovieEditor` previews the picture only, with no sound.

`Narration` holds what the films say, recorded ahead of time and compressed to about 8 KB a second, so that nobody who watches needs a voice model. `MoviePlayer::narration` and `MovieAssistant::narration` play it in place of the system's voice, which still says whatever has no recording.

2039.docs:
Plays a [`Movie`] as an interactive manual.

Whoever watches can pause, drag the position, jump to a chapter and click the
marks on the film. With "stop at each step" on, which is how it starts, the
film holds at each [`Recorder::guide`](crate::Recorder::guide) until the marked spot is clicked,
so people follow it at their own pace. It sleeps while paused.

Cloning a film is cheap, since the film itself is shared:

```no_run
use ravenrs_movie::{Movie, MoviePlayer};

let movie = Movie::from_bytes(&std::fs::read("manual.ravenmovie").unwrap_or_default())?;
let player = MoviePlayer::new(movie).width(960.0);
# Ok::<(), ravenrs_movie::MovieError>(())
```

conta" read as the same thing twice. Only steps are kept when nothing else came up.

2004.name: NextFilm
2004.docs: The film offered at the end: its name and what opening it does.

1223.name: start_marking
1223.docs: Hides the dialog to mark the page behind it.

669.name: add_overlay
669.docs: Adds an effect at the playhead and selects it.

2077.name: go_to_film
2077.docs: Opens a film of a [`MovieAssistant`](crate::MovieAssistant)'s library at `ms`.

2177.name: FilmSounds
2177.docs: The sounds a film makes, computed once for each player.

2831.name: type_into
2831.docs: Clicks the field called `name` and types `text` into it, letter by letter.

188.name: MOMENTS
188.docs: How many moments an answer offers.

2277.name: logo
2277.docs: The app's animated logo, played on the film's opening and farewell cards.

1823.name: with_project
1823.docs: The same film with these edits.

1596.name: Stored
1596.docs: One thing the app drew, in as few characters as a file can have it.

1142.name: BugLabels
1142.docs: The words a [`BugReporter`] shows. English by default.

2023.name: SOUNDS_AT_MOST_MS
2023.docs:
A frame that came late plays only what is this recent: a burst of clicks
after a pause would tell nothing.

2123.name: advance
2123.docs:
Moves to where the clock says it should be. The first stop crossed on the
way holds it there, and the end of the film finishes it.

2450.name: speed
2450.docs: 1 is real time, 2 is twice as fast. Cards ignore it.

2777.name: NotOnScreen
2777.docs: The script names something that is not on the screen.

107.name: narration
107.docs: Recordings of what the films say, in place of the system's voice.

3077.name: root
3077.docs:
A word without the plural and the usual endings of verbs, so "pago", "pague"
and "pagar" meet. This is not a real stemmer: it only has to bring near forms
together, and a root under three letters is left alone.

1969.name: new
1969.docs:
Reads what [`Narration::pack`] wrote. Bytes it does not understand hold no
recordings, and the films use the system's voice.

2723.name: insert_card
2723.docs: A [`Self::insert_title`] of a `look`: an opening at 0, a farewell at the end.

1842.name: from_bytes
1842.docs: Reads a film back from the bytes of a file.

1361.name: HotspotKind
1361.docs: What a spot on the screen does.

1134.name: mark_again
1134.docs: The same button, when a box was already drawn.

2015.name: BOX_WIDTH
2015.docs:
The box that explains what is being done, and the film width it needs to fit:
on a smaller film the same words go under it.

2115.name: Playhead
2115.docs:
Where a film is, read and written while building. Clicks raise `changes`, so
the player rebuilds; while playing, it asks to be woken for the next picture.

453.name: tab_interaction
453.docs: The tool tab with clickable spots.

2869.name: FAR_BELOW_THE_BEST
2869.docs: An answer far weaker than the best one is noise.

653.name: new
653.docs: Starts editing `movie`, with whatever edits it already has.

980.name: stretch
980.docs:
The stretch being written, starting another when this one is full. Two
stretches of half the time each always hold at least that half, and old
memory goes all at once instead of frame by frame.

99.name: MovieCue

299.name: composition
299.docs: One moment of an edited film, drawn: the film, then everything over it.

626.name: trying
626.docs: The canvas shows the player, the way people will watch.

1834.name: draw_list
1834.docs: What the app drew at this moment of the film.

2715.name: delete_clip
2715.docs:
Takes a clip out and closes the gap: overlays after it come along, those
over it get shorter, and those only over it go.

399.name: moving_card
399.docs:
An opening or a farewell: two soft lights drift on the app's color, the logo
plays, and the words come in one after the other, rising a little.

2488.name: Label
2488.docs: A filled label in the accent color.

1934.name: Adpcm
1934.docs: Where the ADPCM decoder stands. The encoder follows the same path.

1053.name: BugReport
1053.docs: What someone says about a bug, for the development team.

2815.name: Recorder
2815.docs:
Runs an app from a script and films it: the steps are the ones a person would
take, found by the names screen readers see. See the [crate documentation](crate).

2034.name: language
2034.docs: The language of the voice, such as `pt-BR`.

145.name: moment_row
145.docs: A row that says which moment an answer is and opens it.

2007.name: SPEEDS
2007.docs: How fast a film can play.

672.name: add_title
672.docs: Puts a title card at the playhead and selects it.

445.name: try_it
445.docs: Tries the film the way people will watch it.

2534.name: at_ms
2534.docs: When it starts on the timeline, in milliseconds.

2861.name: TITLE_WEIGHT
2861.docs: How much a word counts in each part of a moment.

2407.name: to_ms
2407.docs: Where it ends in the film, in milliseconds.

2834.name: scroll
2834.docs:
Rolls the wheel over what is under the pointer, `pixels` in all; positive
goes down the page.

191.name: intro
191.docs: What it says before the first question.

2280.name: cue
2280.docs: Lets something outside the player open a moment of the film.

391.name: new
391.docs: The moment `at_ms` of the timeline of `movie`.

1045.name: kinds
1045.docs: The kinds of report to choose from. The first starts chosen.

2580.name: Hide
2580.docs: Covers this region, for what the film should not show.

237.name: examples
237.docs: Things to ask, offered before the first question.

1218.name: new
1218.docs: A reporter over what `recorder` keeps; `on_send` gets the finished report.

664.name: toggle_playing
664.docs: Plays from the playhead, or pauses.

110.name: MovieChat

1972.name: seconds
1972.docs: How long the recording of `text` lasts, in seconds, without decoding it.

864.name: RecentErrors

310.name: to_screen
310.docs: A point of the film, on the screen.

183.name: MovieWriter
183.docs:
Writes an answer about the moments that a question found. It gets the question,
the moments, where to write the text, what to do when the text moves, and what
to write if it fails. See [`MovieChat::writer`].

2826.name: intro
2826.docs:
Starts a chapter here and explains it in a box in the middle of the film,
for as long as it takes to read or hear.

2272.name: new
2272.docs: A player for `movie`, stopped at its first picture.

937.name: MARKING_DIM
937.docs: How much the page dims while marking: enough to tell the mode, not to hide the page.

1137.name: elements
1137.docs: Before the elements under the box.

2118.name: go_on
2118.docs:
Goes on from the step it is waiting at, past the time the step would take
for whoever is not stopping at steps.

1010.name: film
1010.docs: The film so far, to look at, edit or send. Recording goes on.

456.name: track_film
456.docs: The film's row on the timeline.

2872.name: Step
2872.docs: A step that waits for a click.

656.name: edit
656.docs: Makes an edit. Edits with the same `key` in a row count as one undo.

1964.name: key_of
1964.docs: The same number on every run and every machine, for finding a text.

1410.name: until_ms
1410.docs: When it goes away, in milliseconds.

2718.name: set_speed
2718.docs: Changes how fast a clip plays, which moves what comes after it.

1283.name: movie
1283.docs: A film in memory and in a file: what the app drew, each thing stored once.

1056.name: MovieError
1056.docs: What can go wrong with a film.

2818.name: narration
2818.docs:
The recordings the player will say the boxes with. Each box then lasts as
long as its recording, and a little more, so that the voice and the box
end together and the film never ends while the voice is still speaking.
A box with no recording lasts as long as reading it takes.

1256.name: named_under
1256.docs:
The names on screen under `area`, in reading order and once each. What is more
than half outside it is left out, or the panels around it would always count.

2110.name: waiting
2110.docs: The stop it is waiting at.

1883.name: new
1883.docs: A film of an app of this logical size, over this color.

94.name: MovieLibrary

748.name: OVERLAY_IDS
748.docs: The ids blocks have on the timeline: clips below, overlays above.

194.name: MovieChatLabels
194.docs: The words a [`MovieChat`] shows. English by default.

1175.name: light
1175.docs: What lights the marked box in the film, to replace when it is marked again.

1829.name: chapters
1829.docs:
Its chapters, on the edited timeline. A chapter that was cut starts where
the cut left it, unless nothing of it remains.

2710.name: clip_start_ms
2710.docs: When a clip starts on the timeline.

394.name: logo
394.docs:
The app's animated logo, which plays on the opening and the farewell cards
([`CardLook`]), in the time of the film: it follows a pause or a jump.

3037.name: get
3037.docs: The film at `index`, with its title.

1048.name: area
1048.docs: The box they drew around the problem, in the logical pixels of the window.

821.name: on_save
821.docs: Shows a save button that runs `handler` with the film and its edits.

2910.name: film
2910.docs: The film, by its position in the library.

267.name: on_open
267.docs: What opening a moment means in the app.

2356.name: Plain
2356.docs: The title and the line under it, still.

13.name: AssistantLabels
13.docs: The words a [`MovieAssistant`] shows. English by default.

1221.name: open
1221.docs: Opens the dialog, with the film up to now.

667.name: select_clip
667.docs: Selects the clip at this place on the main track.

1975.name: pack_onto
1975.docs:
What [`Narration::pack`] wrote in `bytes`, with `recordings` added. What is in
`bytes` stays exactly as it was, so that adding a few texts after a film changed
keeps the takes chosen before; a text in both is the new recording. Bytes it does
not understand count as no recordings.

2075.name: new
2075.docs: A cue that asks for nothing yet.

313.name: Region
313.docs: A rectangle on the film, in the logical pixels of the app.

2829.name: move_to
2829.docs: Slides the pointer to the middle of what is called `name`.

2275.name: max_film_height
2275.docs:
The film is no taller than this, and the chapters take the width it leaves.
For a player that should fit a window with its controls in view.

1894.name: hotspot
1894.docs: Adds a spot on the screen.

5.name: AROUND_THE_FILM
5.docs: What goes around the film: the question, the choice of film and the controls.

105.name: width
105.docs: The width of the whole assistant, in logical pixels (960 by default).

759.name: RegionHandle
759.docs: The selected region on the canvas, to drag and resize.

1967.name: narration
1967.docs:
Recordings of what the film says, in place of the system's voice. What is not
among them is still said by the system's voice.

1413.name: is_general
1413.docs:
Whether it talks about the screen as a whole, with no spot to mark. It
has no size, and its box shows in the middle of the film.

859.name: KEPT
859.docs: How many it keeps: what led to a bug is in the last ones.

2948.name: score
2948.docs: How well it answers, comparable only within one search.

305.name: WORDS_RISE
305.docs: How far a line rises as it comes in, in logical pixels of a 960-wide film.

1840.name: click_before
1840.docs: The last click at or before this moment of the film, and how long ago it was.

1286.name: Damaged
1286.docs: The file is not a film, or it was cut short.

2821.name: tick
2821.docs: Advances the clock by one frame and notes what the app draws.

2040.name: from_texts
2040.docs: The texts of a catalog, in its language. What it does not have comes from English.

932.name: flight
932.docs:
The last minutes on screen, always at hand, and a bug report made from them.

Nothing here leaves the computer by itself. What is recorded stays in memory
until someone opens a report, sees the film, covers what should not show and
chooses to send it, through whatever the app does with [`BugReport`].

1359.name: Stop
1359.docs: The film stops here until someone clicks the spot.

2113.name: jumped
2113.docs: The film jumped: what the voice was saying no longer applies.

678.name: Clip
678.docs: One piece of the main track.

2767.name: record
2767.docs: Records a film by running the real app from a script, with no window.

2867.name: CHAPTER_BONUS
2867.docs: A chapter begins the lesson, so it goes ahead of a step that says the same.

2413.name: Title
2413.docs: A card with a title, between stretches of the film.

624.name: density
624.docs: Pixels of the timeline per second.

1832.name: hotspots
1832.docs: Its hotspots, on the edited timeline.

2713.name: film_to_timeline
2713.docs: Where a moment of the film ended up on the timeline; `None` if it was cut.

3040.name: ask
3040.docs:
The moments that best answer `question`, the best first, at most `limit`.
Accents and case do not matter, and near forms of a word count for less:
"pago" finds "pagar". With no word in common, there is no answer.

1051.name: film
1051.docs: The film of what led to it, if they chose to include it.

497.name: EditorLabels
497.docs: The words a [`MovieEditor`] shows. English by default.

270.name: MovieAnswers
270.docs: What answering a question about the films takes. See [`MovieAnswers::answer`].

2032.name: sound
2032.docs: Turns on the sound of clicks and keys.

2359.name: words_in_ms
2359.docs: When the words of a card of this look are all in, in milliseconds from its start.

2005.name: player
2005.docs: Plays a film, stops where it teaches, and lets the watcher jump around.

1451.name: FilmSound
1451.docs: A sound a film makes by itself.

1224.name: finish_marking
1224.docs: Keeps the box drawn, names what is under it and lights it in the film.

443.name: NEW_EFFECT_MS
443.docs: How long a new effect lasts, in milliseconds.

1324.name: Chapter
1324.docs: A part of the film, in the list of chapters.

2078.name: take_film
2078.docs: The film someone asked for, once.

189.name: chat
189.docs: The training films as a conversation: each answer is a card with the moments.

2278.name: card_said
2278.docs:
What an opening or a farewell card says at `at`, once its words are coming
in: told apart from the boxes by a number of its own. Only a recording says
it, since the system's voice would be a second voice in the film.

2151.name: Narrator
2151.docs: Stops the voice when the player leaves the screen.

1924.name: narration
1924.docs:
A film's narration recorded ahead of time: nobody who watches needs a voice model, or
a good system voice. Each text is kept once, compressed to a quarter of its size.

489.name: wait_for_click
489.docs: A hotspot waits for a click.

1143.name: from_texts
1143.docs: The texts of a catalog, in its language. What it does not have comes from English.

2451.name: duration_ms
2451.docs: How long it lasts on the timeline.

8.name: nothing_found
8.docs: When no film answers the question.

662.name: position_ms
662.docs: Where the playhead is, in milliseconds of the timeline.

108.name: logo
108.docs: The app's animated logo, played on the films' opening and farewell cards.

1870.name: edited_marks
1870.docs:
Chapters and hotspots, moved to where the edits put them, with the hotspots
added on the timeline.

3078.name: one_edit_apart
3078.docs: One letter wrong, missing, extra, or two swapped: the usual slips of typing.

1970.name: clip
1970.docs: The recording of `text`, if there is one.

2724.name: add_overlay
2724.docs: Adds an overlay on the first track free for its time, and says which it is.

2824.name: wait
2824.docs: Lets the film run with nothing happening.

935.name: SMALLEST_MARK
935.docs: A smaller box is a click that slipped, not a choice.

2670.name: Title
2670.docs: The card that is this clip.

354.name: camera_at
354.docs:
Where the camera is at `at_ms`, for a screen `width` wide. With `whole`, zooms
do not count, which is how the editor places them.

1889.name: frame
1889.docs:
Adds what the app draws at `at_ms`. Nothing is added when it is the same
as the last time: that picture just stays longer on screen.

2870.name: STOP_WORDS
2870.docs: Words that say nothing about the subject, folded, in Portuguese and English.
